mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week improvement in WORKPLACES mobility (rising from -42.4% to -25.6% over four weeks) signals progressive workplace reopening. This restores commuting routines and incidental retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 16.8 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 5 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: High PARKS mobility (65.0% at t-0w) reflects outdoor recreation preference during pandemic uncertainty. As PARKS demand saturates, substitution occurs toward indoor retail-and-recreation venues, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds 60 percentage points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at t-0w is 65.0%, highest in the four-week window
regime_hint: steady state with high outdoor mobility
failure_condition: PARKS remains above 60% and RETAIL_REC does not increase week-on-week in at least 2 of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility recovery (from -46.4% to -26.1% over four weeks) enables access to retail districts. Coupled with WORKPLACES recovery, restored transit-dependent shopping patterns drive RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves more than 5 percentage points week-on-week AND WORKPLACES improves simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 20.3 points from t-3w to t-0w
fact:WORKPLACES improved 16.8 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES declines by more than 3 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not show positive trend over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent RESIDENTIAL elevation (1.4% to 5.1% over four weeks) indicates ongoing stay-at-home behavior despite workplace reopening. This suppresses retail mobility as home-based consumption substitutes for in-person shopping, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 1% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL elevated at 5.1% at t-3w and 1.4% at t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 0% and RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC deficits (both improving from t-3w to t-0w) reflects coordinated essential-and-discretionary shopping trips. As GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes near baseline, discretionary retail demand accelerates, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM deficit narrows to within 10 percentage points of baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at t-0w is -9.4%, near baseline
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM deficit widens by more than 3 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not improve week-on-week in at least one of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Spring season (mid-September in Southern Hemisphere) drives outdoor recreation preference, evidenced by PARKS at 65.0%. Seasonal shift toward outdoor activity crowds out indoor retail, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks despite workplace recovery.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above 50 percentage points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at t-1w and t-0w are 55.0% and 65.0% respectively
failure_condition: PARKS falls below 40% and RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Negative TRANSIT mobility (-26.1% at t-0w) constrains retail access despite workplace recovery. Insufficient public transport capacity limits footfall to retail districts, preventing RETAIL_REC from rising above current depressed levels over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at t-0w is -26.1%, still substantially below baseline
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves to above -15 percentage points and RETAIL_REC increases by more than 10 percentage points over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Three-way interaction: WORKPLACES recovery enables commuting, TRANSIT improvement enables access, and PARKS saturation redirects discretionary time toward indoor retail. Combined effect drives RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks only if all three conditions align.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves >10 points AND TRANSIT improves >10 points AND PARKS remains >50 points
evidence_refs: fact:All three series show improvement or elevation over the four-week window
failure_condition: Any one of the three proxies reverses by more than 5 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not show sustained improvement over the next 28 days.
